zh: 他请教的不是别人，是王有龄。“题招牌我还是破题儿第一遭。”王有龄笑道，“还不知怎么题法，有些什么讲究？”“第一要响亮，容易上口，第二字眼要与众不同，省得跟别家搅不清楚。至于要跟钱庄有关，要吉利，那当然用不着说了。““好，我来想想看。”他实在有些茫然，随便抽了本书，想先选几个字写下来，然后再来截搭选配。书架上抽出来的那本书是《华阳国志》，随手一翻，看了几行，巧极了，现成有两个字。“这两个字怎么样？”王有龄提笔写了《华阳国志》上的两句话：“世平道治，民物阜康。”在“阜康”上面打了两个圈。“阜康，阜康！”胡雪岩念了两遍，欣然答道，“好极！既阜且康，就是它。”
en: The person he consulted was none other than Wang. “This is my first attempt at naming a business,” Wang laughed. “I don't even know how to begin. What are the requirements?” “First, it must sound impressive and be easy to say. Second, the characters must be distinctive, so nobody confuses it with another firm. Naturally, it must suit a bank and be auspicious.” “Very well. Let me think.” He was rather at a loss. Taking a book at random, he intended to select a few characters, write them down, and then try different combinations. The volume he pulled from the shelf was the Chronicles of Huayang. He opened it and read a few lines. By a fortunate coincidence, two characters lay ready to hand. “What about these?” He wrote out a passage: “The age is peaceful, the way well governed; the people and their possessions flourish in abundance and well-being.” He circled the characters fu and kang. “Fukang, Fukang!” Hu repeated the name twice, then answered gladly, “Excellent! Both abundance and well-being. That's the one.”

zh: 说着，他就要起身辞去，王有龄唤住他说，“雪岩，我有个消息告诉你，我要补实缺了。”“喔！哪个州县？”“现在还不晓得。抚院的刘二来通知我，黄抚台约我今天晚上见面，他顺便透露的消息。照我想，也该补我的缺了。”就这时只见窗外人影闪过，脚步极其匆遽，胡雪岩眼尖，告诉王有龄说：“是吴委员。”门帘掀处，伸进一张笑脸来，等双脚跨进，吴委员就势便请了个安，高声说道，“替大人道喜，真正大喜！”“喔，喔，”王有龄愣了一下，旋即会意，吴委员跟藩署接近，必是有了放缺的消息，便站起身来，连连拱手：“多谢，多谢！”“我刚从藩署来，”他走近两步说，“确确实实的消息，委大人署理湖州府，”这一说，连不十分熟悉官场情形的胡雪岩都觉得诧异，候补州县，“本班”的实缺不曾当过一天，忽然一跃而被委署知府，这不是太离谱了吗？王有龄自然更难置信，“这，这似乎不大对吧？”他迟疑地问。“决不错！明天就‘挂牌’。”
en: As Hu rose to leave, Wang called him back. “Xueyan, I have news. I'm to receive a regular appointment.” “Oh! Which department or county?” “I don't know yet. Liu Er from the governor's office came to say that Governor Huang wishes to see me this evening. He let the news slip. I suppose it is time I received a post.” Just then a figure hurried past the window. Hu's sharp eyes recognised him. “It's Commissioner Wu.” The curtain lifted to reveal a smiling face. As Wu stepped inside, he saluted and announced loudly, “Congratulations, Your Honour! Wonderful news!” Wang paused, then understood. Wu had connections at the provincial treasury and must have heard of the appointment. He stood and repeatedly clasped his hands. “Thank you!” “I've just come from the treasurer's office,” Wu said, stepping closer. “The news is certain: you are to act as prefect of Huzhou.” Even Hu, who knew comparatively little of official practice, was astonished. An expectant department or county magistrate, who had not served a single day in a regular post of his own grade, was suddenly to leap to an acting prefecture? Surely that was extraordinary. Wang found it still harder to believe. “That... that doesn't sound quite right.” “There can be no mistake! The appointment will be posted tomorrow.”

zh: 王有龄沉吟了一会，总觉得事有蹊跷，便央求吴委员再去打听究竟，一面又叫高升到刘二那里去问一问，或者倒有确实消息。消息来得太突兀，却也太令人动心，王有龄患得患失之心大起，在海运局签押房，坐立不宁，胡雪岩便劝他说：“雪公，你沉住了气！照我想，就不是知府，也一定是个大县。到晚上见了抚台就知道了。”“我在想，”王有龄答非所问，“那天藩台说的话，当时我没有在意，现在看来有点道理。”“麟藩台怎么说？”“他先说湖州知府误漕撤任，找不着人去接替，后来说是‘有个主意’，但马上又觉得自己的主意不好，自言自语在说，什么‘办不通’、‘不行’，‘没有这个规矩’。莫非就与刚才这个消息有关？”“那就对了！”胡雪岩拍着自己的大腿说，“不是藩台保荐，抚台顺水推舟，就是抚台交下来，藩台乐得做人情。现在等高升回来，看刘二怎么说？如果藩台刚上院见过抚台，这消息就有八成靠得住了。““说得有理。”王有龄大为欣慰。
en: Wang considered, still feeling that something was strange. He begged Wu to inquire further and sent Gao to ask Liu Er, who might have definite information. The news was both abrupt and intensely exciting. Torn between hope and fear, Wang could neither sit nor stand comfortably in his office. Hu urged him to remain calm. “Even if it isn't a prefecture, it must be a large county. You'll know when you see the governor tonight.” “I was thinking...” Wang's answer followed his own thoughts. “I paid little attention to what the treasurer said the other day. Now it seems significant.” “What did he say?” “First, that Huzhou's prefect had been dismissed for delaying the grain and that no replacement could be found. Then he said he had an idea, but immediately rejected it, muttering that it wouldn't work, that there was no precedent. Could it be connected with this news?” “Then that explains it!” Hu slapped his thigh. “Either the treasurer recommended you and the governor agreed, or the governor proposed it and the treasurer was happy to oblige. Let's hear what Liu Er tells Gao. If the treasurer has just been to see the governor, the news is eight-tenths certain.” “That makes sense.” Wang was greatly reassured.

zh: “不过，雪公！”胡雪岩说，“湖州大户极多，公事难办得很。”“就是这话罗！所以，雪岩，你还是要帮我，跟我一起到湖州去。这句话胡雪岩答应不下，便先宕开一句：“慢慢再商量。雪公，倒是有件事，不可不防！这里的差使怎么样？”“这里”自是指海运局，一句话提醒了王有龄，“坐办”的差使要交卸了，亏空要弥补，经手的公事要交代清楚。后任有后任的办法，倘或海运局的公款不再存信和，关系一断，替松江漕帮借款担保这一层，就会有很大的麻烦，真个不可不防。“是啊！”王有龄吸着气说，“这方面关系甚重，得要早早想办法，我想，跟抚台老实说明白，最好仍旧让我兼这个差使。就怕他说，人在湖州，省城的公事鞭长莫及，那就煞费周章了。”“雪公，我倒要问一句，到了鱼与熊掌不可兼得的那一步，你怎样打算？”“我情愿不补实缺，把这里先顾住。”王有龄说，“我靠朋友帮忙，才有今天，不能留下一个累来害你和张胖子、尤老五！”“雪公！”胡雪岩深深点头，一个字，一个字他说道：“有了这个念头，就不怕没有朋友。”经此一番交谈，王有龄彻底了解了自己的最后立场，心倒反而定了来了。
en: “But remember, Mr Xuexuan: Huzhou has a great many powerful households. Its affairs are very difficult.” “Exactly! That's why you must still help me and come with me.” Hu could not agree to that. He put it aside for the moment. “We can discuss it later. There's another matter we must guard against. What happens to your assignment here?” “Here” meant the Sea Transport Bureau. The question reminded Wang of all that handing over its executive directorship would involve: the deficit must be made good and every affair under his management explained. A successor would have his own methods. If the bureau's funds ceased to be deposited with Xinhe and the relationship ended, their guarantee for the Songjiang association's loan could create serious trouble. It was indeed a danger to consider. “Yes!” Wang drew a breath. “A great deal depends on that. We must act early. I think I should tell the governor frankly and ask to retain the bureau as an additional duty. But if he says I couldn't manage provincial-capital business from Huzhou, we'll be in considerable difficulty.” “Then let me ask you this. If you reach the point where you can't have both, what will you choose?” “I'd rather decline the regular appointment and preserve our position here. I owe my present standing to my friends' help. I can't leave a burden that harms you, Zhang, and You.” Hu nodded deeply and spoke word by word. “With that principle, you'll never lack friends.” Having clarified his ultimate position, Wang felt calmer.

zh: 两个人接着便根据不同的情况，商量在见黄宗汉时，如何措同。这样谈了有半个时辰，高升首先回来复命，如胡雪岩所意料的，这天一早，黄宗汉待为把麟桂找了去，有所密谈，可见得吴委员的消息，不是无因而至。不久，吴委员带回来更详细的喜信，王有龄是被委署为乌程县知县，兼署湖州府知府。事到如今，再无可疑。海运局上上下下，也都得到了消息，约齐了来向坐办贺喜，又商量凑公份办戏酒，为王有龄开贺。这大招摇了！王有龄一定不肯，托吴委员向大家道谢疏通，千万不可有此举动。扰攘半日，莫衷一是，他也只得暂且丢下不问，准时奉召去看黄宗汉。
en: They discussed how he should address Huang under various circumstances. After about an hour, Gao returned. As Hu had expected, Huang had specially summoned Lingui that morning for a private consultation. Wu's news plainly had a basis. Soon Wu himself brought fuller confirmation: Wang was to act as magistrate of Wucheng County and concurrently as prefect of Huzhou. There could be no further doubt. Everyone at the bureau had heard and came together to congratulate their director. They also discussed subscribing for a feast and theatrical performance in his honour. Wang thought this far too ostentatious and firmly refused. He asked Wu to thank them and make absolutely clear that no such celebration should be held. Half a day of commotion produced no agreement. At last he put the matter aside and went punctually to the governor's summons.

zh: “今年的钱粮，一定要想办法征足，军费浩繁，催京饷的部文，接二连三飞到，你看，还有一道上谕。”王有龄起身从黄宗汉手中上谕来看，只见洋洋千言，尽是有关筹饷和劝谕捐输的指示，最后一段说：“户部现因外省拨款，未能如期解到，奏请将俸银分别暂停一年。朕思王公大臣，俸人素优，即暂停给发，事尚可行，其文职四品以下，武职三品以下各员，仍着户部将本看春季暂停俸银，照数补行给领。并着发内库帑银五十万两，交部库收存，以备支放俸饷要需。”王公大臣的俸银，岂肯长此停发？当然要严催各省解款。王有龄心有警惕，今年的州县官，对于征粮一事，要看得比什么都重。“本省的钱粮，全靠杭、嘉、湖三府，湖州尤其是命脉所在。我跟麟藩台商量，非你去不可。时逢二百年来未有之变局，朝廷一再申谕，但求实效，不借破格用人。所以保你老兄署湖州府，我想不至于被驳。”王有龄是早就预备好了的，听黄宗汉一口气说下来，语声暂停之际，赶快起身请安：“大人这样子栽培，真是叫人感激涕零，惶恐万分，不知如何报答？““要谈报答，只要把公事办妥了就是报答。湖州地方，与众不同，雪轩兄，你要把全副本事拿出来。”“是！”王有龄紧接着说，“不过我有下情，还要大人格外体恤。”“你说。只要于公事有益，无不可通融。”
en: “We must find a way to collect this year's full revenue. Military expenses are enormous. Ministry dispatches demanding remittances to the capital arrive one after another. Look—another edict.” Wang rose and took the document from Huang. Its lengthy text concerned raising military funds and encouraging contributions. The final passage read: “As provincial appropriations have failed to arrive on schedule, the Board of Revenue proposes suspending salary payments for one year, according to rank. We consider that princes and senior ministers have long enjoyed generous emoluments, so a temporary suspension is practicable. For civil officials below the fourth rank and military officials below the third, however, let the Board pay in full the salaries withheld this spring. Let five hundred thousand taels also be released from the privy treasury into the Board's treasury to meet essential salary and military expenditure.” Would princes and senior ministers tolerate a prolonged interruption of their salaries? Naturally, the provinces would face relentless demands for funds. Wang took warning: this year, local officials must give revenue collection precedence over everything. “Our province depends on Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou, with Huzhou its particular lifeblood,” Huang continued. “Treasurer Lin and I have agreed that you must go. In this crisis, unparalleled in two hundred years, the court has repeatedly urged practical results and exceptional appointments where necessary. I therefore doubt it will reject my recommendation that you act as prefect.” Wang was prepared. As soon as Huang paused, he rose and saluted. “Such favour overwhelms me with gratitude and apprehension. I don't know how to repay it.” “Handle the public business properly, and that will be repayment enough. Huzhou is unlike other places, Brother Xuexuan. You must bring all your ability to bear.” “Yes. But there is a personal difficulty for which I must ask your special consideration.” “Speak. Anything that benefits the public business can be accommodated.”

zh: “这是海运局的公事。”王有龄说，“我接手还不久，这次‘民折官办’一案，其中委曲，无不在大人洞鉴之中。如今首尾未了倘或后任不明究竟，遇事挑剔，且不说赔累的话，只往来申复解释，就极费功夫。大人请想，那时我人在湖州，如何得能全副心思去对付钱粮。这后顾之忧，我斗胆要请大人作主。”“你要我如何替你作主？”黄宗汉问。“请大人许我在这一案了结以后再交卸。”黄宗汉沉吟了，两眼望空，似乎有所盘算。这一个便也猜他的心思，莫非这个差使已经许了别人，所以为难？“答应你兼差，原无不可。”黄宗汉慢慢把视线落在他脸上，“只是你兼顾得来吗？”这一问在王有龄意料之中，随即答道：“请大人放心，一定兼顾得来。因为我部下有个人非常得力，这一次‘民折官办’，如果没有他多方联络折冲，不能这么顺利。“
en: “It concerns the Sea Transport Bureau. I've only recently taken charge. Your Excellency understands every complication of the official-procurement arrangement. Matters are still unfinished. If a successor, unaware of the circumstances, objects at every turn, then even apart from possible financial liabilities, the correspondence needed to explain and justify everything would consume enormous time. With me in Huzhou, how could I devote my full attention to revenue collection? I venture to ask you to remove this concern.” “What would you have me do?” “Allow me to hand over only after this affair has been concluded.” Huang fell silent, gazing into space as though calculating. Wang tried to read his thoughts. Had the post already been promised to someone else? “There is no objection in principle to your holding both duties,” Huang said slowly, bringing his eyes back to Wang. “But can you manage them?” The question was expected. “Rest assured, I can. I have an exceptionally capable man under me. Without his work in making contacts and negotiating on every side, the procurement affair could never have proceeded so smoothly.”

zh: “喔，这个人叫什么名字？是什么出身？几时带来我看看。”“此人叫胡光墉，年纪甚轻，虽是阛阓中人，实在是个奇才。眼前尚无功名，似乎不便来谒见大人。”“那也不要紧。现在有许多事要办，只要是人才，不怕不能出头。黄宗汉问，”你说他是阛阓中人，做的什么买卖？““他，”王有龄替胡雪岩吹牛，“他是钱业世家，家道殷实，现在自己设了个钱庄。”“钱庄？好，很好，很好！”一连说了三个“好”字，语气奇怪，王有龄倒有些担心，觉得皮里阳秋，用意难测，不能不留神。“提起钱庄，我倒想起一件事来了。”黄宗汉问，“现在京朝大吏，各省督抚，纷纷捐输军饷，我亦不能不勉为其难，想凑个一万银子出来，略尽绵薄。过几天托那姓胡的钱庄，替我汇一汇。”“是！”王有龄答道：“理当效劳，请大人随时交下来就是了。”
en: “Oh? What is his name? What qualifications does he hold? Bring him to see me sometime.” “His name is Hu Guangyong. He is young, and though a man of commerce, he has extraordinary abilities. At present he holds no official or scholarly qualification, so it may not be proper for him to seek an audience.” “That doesn't matter. There is much to be done. A talented man need not fear being overlooked. What business is he in?” “He...” Wang exaggerated on Hu's behalf. “He comes from a prosperous banking family and has now established a bank of his own.” “A bank? Good. Very good indeed!” The repeated approval had a strange tone. Wang feared some concealed implication and grew watchful. “Speaking of banks reminds me of something,” Huang continued. “Senior officials in the capital and governors throughout the provinces are contributing to military funds. I too must make an effort. I intend to assemble ten thousand taels as a modest contribution. In a few days, ask this Mr Hu's bank to remit it for me.” “Certainly. We should be honoured to serve. Please send the money whenever convenient.”

zh: 一听这话，黄宗汉便端茶碗送客，对他兼领海运局的事，并无下文。王有龄心里不免焦急，不上下下，不知再用什么方法，方能讨出一句实话来？因此，他一出抚台衙门，立刻嘱咐高升去找胡雪岩。等他刚刚到家，胡雪岩跟着也就来了，王有龄顾不得换衣服，便拉了他到书房里，关起房门，细说经过。“现在海运局的事，悬在半空里，该怎么打算，竟毫无着手之处，你说急人不急人？”王有龄接着又说，“索性当面告诉我不行。反倒好进一步表明决心，此刻弄得进退维谷了。”“不要紧，事情好办得很。”胡雪岩很随便他说，“再多花几两银子就行了。”“咦！”王有龄说，“我倒不相信，你何以有些把握？再说，花几两银子是花多少，怎么个花法？““雪公！你真正是聪明一世，懵懂一时。‘盘口’已经开出来了，一万银子！”“啊！”王有龄恍然大悟，“怪不得，怪不得！”他把当时的情形又回想了一遍，只因为自己不明其中的奥妙，说了句等他“随时交下来”，黄宗汉一听他不识窍，立刻就端茶送客，真个翻脸无情，想想也不免寒心。
en: At that, Huang lifted his tea bowl, signalling the end of the audience. Nothing further was said about retaining the bureau. Wang was anxious. Left suspended between possibilities, he could not see how to obtain a definite answer. As soon as he left, he sent Gao to find Hu. Hu arrived just after him. Without even changing his clothes, Wang took him into the study, closed the door, and recounted everything. “The bureau is now hanging in mid-air. I don't know where to begin. Isn't that maddening? If he'd simply refused, I could have stated my decision. As it is, I can neither advance nor retreat.” “Never mind. It's very easy,” Hu said casually. “A little more silver will settle it.” “Why, I don't believe you! How can you be so sure? And how much is ‘a little’? How would it be spent?” “Mr Xuexuan, you're clever all your life and muddled for a moment. He's already named his price: ten thousand taels.” “Ah!” Wang understood. “No wonder!” He reconsidered the scene. Because he had failed to grasp the implication, he had asked Huang to send the money at his convenience. Hearing that he had missed the point, Huang had immediately dismissed him. The abrupt coldness was disheartening.

zh: “闲话少说，这件事办得要快，‘药到病除’，不宜耽误！”“当然，当然。”王有龄想了想说：“明天就托信和汇一万银子到部里去。”“慢一点，这一万银子交给我，我另有用处。”这话似乎费解，但王有龄看他不说，也就不问，这是他笼络胡雪岩的方法之一，表示彻底信任，所以点点头说：“明天上午请你到局里来取。”“不！明天雪公一定很忙，我不来打搅，请派个人把银票给我送来，尽上午把它办好，中午我们碰头。”“慢慢，我想一想。”王有龄猜度明天的情况：“算它一早‘挂牌’，立刻就要到藩署谢委，跟着上抚台衙门……”“不！”胡雪岩打断他的话，摇着手说，“雪公，抚台那里下午去。你从藩暑回局里，有件要紧事办，把局里的人找了来，透露点意思给他们，海运局的差使不动。为什么呢？是要把人心稳住，拿钱庄来说，如果档手一调动，伙计们就会到外面去瞎讲，或者别人问到，不能不回话，这样一来，内部许多秘密，就会泄漏出来。我想官场也是一样，所以只要这样一说，人心定了，就不会有风言风语，是是非非。雪公，你看可是？”“怎么不是？”王有龄笑道，“我的脑筋也算很快，不过总比你慢了一步。就这样吧，别的话明天中午碰了头再说。”
en: “No more talk. Act quickly. The right medicine cures the illness; there's no reason to delay.” “Certainly.” Wang considered. “Tomorrow I'll have Xinhe remit ten thousand to the ministry.” “Wait. Give me that money. I have another use for it.” The words were puzzling, but Wang did not ask. Showing complete trust was one of his methods of securing Hu's loyalty. He nodded. “Come to the bureau tomorrow morning to collect it.” “No. You'll be very busy. I won't disturb you. Send the draft to me, and I'll finish the business during the morning. We'll meet at noon.” “Wait, let me think.” Wang anticipated the next day's schedule. “Assuming the appointment is posted early, I'll immediately go to thank the treasurer, then to the governor...” “No.” Hu interrupted and waved his hand. “See the governor in the afternoon. When you return from the treasury, there's something important to do at the bureau. Gather the staff and let them know you're retaining the directorship. Why? To settle their minds. In banking, when a manager changes, the employees begin talking outside, or answer questions they cannot avoid. Many internal secrets escape that way. I imagine official life is the same. Once people feel secure, there'll be no rumours and needless trouble. Don't you agree?” “Of course!” Wang smiled. “My mind is quick enough, but always one step behind yours. We'll do that and discuss the rest at noon.”

zh: 到了第二天十点多钟，海运局的庶务，奉命去打了一张信和的银票送来。胡雪岩随即去找刘庆生。他是这样打算，刘庆生是个可造之村，但是立柜台的伙计，一下子跳成档手，同行难免轻视，要想办法提高他的身分，培养他的资望。现在替黄宗汉去办理汇款，显得来头不小，以一省来说，抚台是天宇第一号的主顾，有这样的大主顾在手里，同行对刘庆生自然会刮目相看。等他说明了这番意思，刘庆生高兴得不得了，但是他倒不尽是为自己高兴。“真正是意想不到的漂亮！”他收敛笑容说，“胡先生，实不相瞒，有句话，我现在可以说了。大源的孙先生，对你老人家的后台、实力，还有点将信将疑。我心里懊恼，苦于无法分辩，空口说白话，毫无用处，不如不说，我现在到大源去办了这笔汇款，他们就晓得你老人家的手面了！”“还有这一层？”胡雪岩笑道，“等招牌挂了出来，看我再耍点手面给他们看看。”“事不宜迟，我此刻就去办。等下我把票据达到府上。”
en: After ten the following morning, the bureau's general affairs officer brought a draft drawn on Xinhe. Hu immediately went to Liu Qingsheng. His reasoning was this: Liu had promise, but his sudden promotion from counter clerk to manager might provoke disdain among fellow bankers. His standing and reputation must be developed. Handling the governor's remittance would demonstrate powerful connections. Within the province, the governor was the foremost possible client. With such a customer, everyone would view Liu differently. Once Hu explained, Liu was delighted—but not merely for himself. “What an unexpectedly splendid opportunity!” Then he grew serious. “Mr Hu, there's something I can tell you now. Mr Sun at Dayuan still doubts your backing and resources. It annoyed me, but I couldn't refute him. Empty words were useless, so I said nothing. If I arrange this remittance through Dayuan, they'll see your influence for themselves.” “So that's how it is?” Hu smiled. “Wait until our signboard is up. I'll show them a little more.” “Then I mustn't delay. I'll do it now and bring the documents to your house afterwards.”

zh: 刘庆生的身价已非昔比了，穿上盐大街估衣铺买来的绸缎袍褂，簇新的鞋袜，雇了一乘小轿，抬到大源。大源的伙计无不注目，以为来了个大主顾，等轿帘打开，一看是刘庆生，个个讶然，自也不免妒羡。刘庆主略略有些窘态，幸好他天生一张笑脸，所以大家也还不忍去挖苦他。见了孙德庆，稍稍有一番寒暄，随即谈入正题：“我有笔款子，想托大源汇到京里，汇到‘日升昌’好了，这家票号跟户部有往来，比较方便。”“多少两？”孙德庆问：“是捐官的银子？”“不是。黄抚台报效的军饷，纹银一万两。”听说是黄抚台的款子，孙德庆的表情立刻不同了，“咦！”他惊异而重视，“庆生，你的本事真不小，抚台的线都搭上了。”“我哪里有这样的本事，另外有人托我的。”“哪个？”刘庆生故意笑笑不响，让他自己去猜，也知道他一定一猜便着，偏要叫他自己说出来才够味。“莫非胡雪岩？”“是的。”刘庆生看着他，慢慢地点一点头，好象在问：这一下你知道他了吧？
en: Liu's standing had changed. He put on a silk robe and jacket bought at a second-hand clothing shop on Yanda Street, added new shoes and socks, and hired a small chair to Dayuan. The employees all looked up, expecting an important customer. When the curtain lifted and revealed Liu, they were astonished, envious, and admiring. He felt a little awkward, but his naturally smiling face made them reluctant to mock him. After a few civilities with Sun, he came to business. “I have a remittance to send to the capital through Dayuan. Send it to Rishengchang. That remittance house deals with the Board of Revenue, which will make things convenient.” “How much? Money to purchase office?” “No. Governor Huang's contribution to military funds: ten thousand taels of standard silver.” Sun's expression changed at once. “Why, Qingsheng!” He was surprised and impressed. “You've done well indeed, reaching the governor's circle.” “I have no such ability. Someone else entrusted it to me.” “Who?” Liu merely smiled, deliberately leaving him to guess. He knew the answer would be immediate but wanted the satisfaction of hearing Sun say it. “Hu Xueyan?” “Yes.” Liu looked at him and slowly nodded, as though asking whether he understood Hu now.

zh: 孙德庆有些困惑而艳羡的表情，把银票拿了出去交柜上办理汇划，随即又走了进来问道：“你们那家号子，招牌定了没有？”“定了，叫‘阜康’。”“阜康！”孙德庆把身子凑了过来，很神秘地问道，“阜康有黄抚台的股子？”他的想法，出人意外，刘庆生心想，这话关系甚重，说出去变成招摇，不要意出是非来，所以立即答道：“我不晓得，想来不会，本省的抚台，怎么可以在本省开钱庄？”“你当然不会晓得，这个内幕……”孙德庆诡秘地笑笑，不再说下去，脸上是那种保有独得之秘的矜持。刘庆生是真的不知道，阜康有没有黄抚台的股份在内？所以无法代为辩白，但总觉得心里有些不安。等把汇票打好，刘庆生离了大源，坐轿来到胡家，一面交差一面把孙德庆的猜测，据实相告。胡雪岩得意地笑了。“让他们去乱猜。市面‘哄’得越大，阜康的生意越好做。”
en: Puzzled and envious, Sun took the draft to the counter for processing, then returned. “Have you settled on a name for your firm?” “Yes. Fukang.” “Fukang!” Sun leaned closer and asked mysteriously, “Does Governor Huang have a share in it?” The notion surprised Liu. It was a serious suggestion. Repeated outside, it could become a boast of official backing and cause trouble. He answered immediately, “I don't know, but I shouldn't think so. How could a provincial governor open a bank in his own province?” “Of course you wouldn't know the inside story...” Sun smiled knowingly and said no more, wearing the reserved expression of a man possessing a private secret. Liu really did not know whether the governor held shares and could not deny it on anyone's behalf. He nevertheless felt uneasy. Once the remittance draft was ready, he took a chair to Hu's house, delivered it, and honestly reported Sun's speculation. Hu smiled with satisfaction. “Let them guess. The more excitement in the market, the easier Fukang's business will be.”

zh: 这一说刘庆主才放心，欣然告辞。胡雪岩随即也到了海运局，只见好几乘轿子在门口。杭州府所治两县：钱塘、仁和，钱塘是首县。县里的差役正在驱散闲人，维持交通。胡雪岩知道贺客正多，便不走大门，从夹弄中的侧门进去，悄悄溜到签押房旁边他平日起坐的那间小屋里。“胡老爷！”伺候签押房的听差李成，笑嘻嘻地报告消息：“我们老爷高升了。”“喔！怎么样？”“补了乌程县，署理湖州府，仍旧兼局里的差使。我们老爷官运亨通，做下人的连带也沾了光。胡老爷，”李成说道：“我有件事想求胡老爷。”“你说，你说！”“我有个表叔，笔下很来得。只为吃了一场官司，光景很惨。我想请胡老爷说说，带了到湖州去。“噢！”胡雪岩问道：“你那表叔笔下来得，是怎么个来得呢？”“写封把应酬信，都说好。也会打算盘记帐，”胡雪岩想了想说：“我倒要先试试他看。你几时叫他来看我。”“是！”李成很兴奋地说，“不知道胡老爷什么时候有空，我叫他来。”
en: Reassured, Liu departed happily. Hu went to the bureau, where several chairs stood outside. Hangzhou's prefectural seat contained two counties, Qiantang and Renhe, with Qiantang the principal one. Its runners were clearing onlookers and managing traffic. Knowing that congratulatory visitors had arrived in numbers, Hu avoided the main entrance, slipped through a side door in the lane, and quietly entered his usual small room beside the private office. “Mr Hu!” Li Cheng, the office attendant, smiled as he delivered the news. “Our master has been promoted.” “Oh? To what?” “Wucheng County, with acting charge of Huzhou Prefecture, while retaining his bureau duties. Our master's official fortune is flourishing, and we servants benefit too. Mr Hu, I have a favour to ask.” “Go on.” “I have an uncle who's very good with his pen. A lawsuit ruined him, and he's in miserable circumstances. Could you put in a word and have him taken to Huzhou?” “Good with his pen in what way?” “People praise his social letters. He can also use an abacus and keep accounts.” Hu considered. “I'd like to try him first. Ask him to come and see me.” “Yes!” Li was excited. “When will you be free?”

zh: 胡雪岩刚要答话，只听靴声囊囊，王有龄的影子已在窗外出现，李成急忙迎了出去打帘子，把主人迎了进来。王有龄却不回签押房，一直来到胡雪岩的那间小屋，只见他春风满面，步属安详，气派似乎大不相同了。“恭喜，恭喜！”胡雪岩含笑起身，兜头一揖。“彼此，彼此！”王有龄拉住他的手说，“到我那里去谈。”他把胡雪岩邀到签押房的套问，并坐在他歇午觉的一张小床上，有着掩抑不住的兴奋，“雪岩！”他说，“一直到今天上午见了藩台，我才能相信。一年工夫不到，实在想不到有今日之下的局面。福者祸所倚，我心里反倒有些嘀咕了。““雪公，你千万要沉住气！今日之果，昨日之因，莫想过去。只看将来。今日之下如何，不要去管它，你只想着今天我做了些什么，该做些什么就是了。“
en: Before Hu could answer, footsteps sounded and Wang's figure appeared outside the window. Li hurried to lift the curtain. Instead of entering his office, Wang came directly into Hu's small room. His face was radiant, his pace composed, and his bearing seemed altogether altered. “Congratulations!” Hu rose with a smile and bowed. “To both of us!” Wang took his hand. “Come and talk in my room.” He led Hu into the inner room of his office, and they sat side by side on the small bed where he took his afternoon rest. His excitement was irrepressible. “Xueyan, I couldn't believe it until I saw the treasurer this morning. Less than a year! Who could have imagined my position today? Misfortune lurks beside good fortune. I'm almost uneasy.” “You must remain steady. Today's result comes from yesterday's causes. Don't dwell on the past; look ahead. Never mind your present standing. Think only of what you've done today and what you ought to do.”

zh: 王有龄听他的话，克制着自己，把心静下来，“第一件事我要跟你商量，”他说，“藩台催我赶快到任，另外有人劝我，赶在五月初一接印，先有一笔现成的节敬好收，你看怎么样？”这一问，把胡雪岩问住了。他细想了想答道：“官场的规矩我不懂，不过人同此心，捡现成要看看，于人无损的现成好捡，不然就是抢人家的好处，要将心比心，自己设身处地，为别人想一想。”“我踌躇的就是这一层。节敬只有一份，我得了，前任署理的就落空了……”“这就决不能要！”胡雪岩打断他的话说，“人家署理了好些日子，该当收此一份节敬，不该去抢他，铜钱银子用得完，得罪一个人要想补救不大容易……”“好，你不必说了。”王有龄也打断了他的话，“我决定端午以后接印。”“那就对了！雪公，你鸿运当头，做事千万要漂亮。”胡雪岩一面说，一面把那张汇票交了给他。
en: Taking his advice, Wang restrained himself and grew calmer. “First, there's something to discuss. The treasurer wants me to take office quickly. Someone else suggests accepting the seal on the first day of the fifth month, so I can collect the festival gifts already due. What do you think?” This baffled Hu. After careful thought, he answered, “I don't know official customs, but human feelings are the same. Before taking a ready-made benefit, consider whether it harms anyone. If it doesn't, well and good. Otherwise you're taking someone else's advantage. Put yourself in his place.” “That's exactly why I hesitate. There's only one set of festival gifts. If I take them, the present acting magistrate loses them...” “Then you absolutely mustn't!” Hu interrupted. “He's held the post for some time and deserves this payment. You shouldn't take it away. Money can be spent, but offending someone isn't easily repaired...” “Enough,” Wang interrupted in turn. “I've decided to receive the seal after the Dragon Boat Festival.” “Exactly. Your fortune is rising. You must handle things handsomely.” As he spoke, Hu handed over the remittance draft.

zh: “这是要紧的，我吃了饭就上院。只怕手本递进去，他没工夫见！”王有龄很认真他说，“这件事非要从速有个了断不可！”“也不一定要见你。‘火到猪头烂’，只要他见了汇票就好了，不妨先写好一封信摆着，见不着人就递信。顺便把抚台衙门节下该开销了，早早开销，那就放心好了，自会有人送消息来。”“不错，准定这么办。”王有龄略停一下又说：“雪岩，这一补了实缺，起码又要万把银子垫进去，窟窿越扯越大，我有点担心呢！”“不要怕，有我！”胡雪岩催他，“事不宜迟，最好趁黄抚台不曾打中觉以前就去一趟。”
en: “This is important. I'll go to the governor after lunch. But even if I send in my card, he may have no time to see me.” Wang was earnest. “This must be settled promptly.” “He needn't necessarily see you. Enough heat will cook the pig's head: he only needs to see the draft. Write a letter beforehand and send that in if you can't get an audience. While you're there, distribute the customary festival gifts in his office early. Then you can rest easy; someone will bring news.” “Yes, that's what I'll do.” Wang paused. “Xueyan, taking up a regular post will mean advancing another ten thousand taels or so. The hole grows bigger and bigger. I'm worried.” “Don't be. You have me. Don't delay—go before the governor takes his nap.”

zh: 王有龄依他的话办，写好一封短简，把汇票封在里面，又备好节下该开发的赏号，一一用红封套套好，一大叠揣在靴页子里，然后传轿到抚台衙门。刘二一见，赶来道喜。王有龄今非昔比，不免要摆一摆架子，但架了摆在脸上，赏封捏在手里，一个二十两银票的红封套塞了过去，那就架上摆得越足，刘二便越发恭敬。“王大老爷！”刘二用那种极显决心的语气说，“今天是不是要见抚台？要见，我一定让你老见着！““怎么呢？抚台极忙？”“是啊！不是极忙，我怎么说这话？”刘二低声说道，“京里来了人，在签押房里关上门谈了一上午了。将军也派了‘戈什哈’来请，说有军务要商量，这一去，说不定到晚才能回来。如果王大老爷一定要见，我此刻就上去回，掉个枪花，总要让你老见着。不过，就见了也谈不到多少时候。““那么，抚台去拜将军之前，可有看封信的工夫？”“这一定有的。你老把信交给我，我伺候在旁边，一定让他拆开来看。”王有龄便把信交了给他：“那就拜托你了。抚台有什么话，劳驾你跑一趟，给我个信。”“那不用说的，我自然晓得。”
en: Wang followed the advice. He wrote a short letter, enclosed the draft, and prepared the festival gratuities, each in a red envelope. With a thick stack tucked inside his boot flap, he called for his chair and went to the governor's yamen. Liu Er hurried over with congratulations. Wang's standing had changed, and he could not resist assuming some importance. But while dignity showed on his face, a reward was ready in his hand. Once he passed over an envelope containing a twenty-tael note, the grander his manner, the more respectful Liu became. “Your Honour,” Liu said with great determination, “do you want to see the governor today? If you do, I'll make certain of it.” “Why? Is he very busy?” “Indeed. Otherwise I wouldn't say so.” Liu lowered his voice. “Someone has come from the capital. They've been behind closed doors in the private office all morning. The garrison general has also sent an orderly asking him over to discuss military affairs. Once he goes, he may not return until evening. If you must see him, I'll announce you now and contrive something. But even if you get in, there won't be much time.” “Before he visits the general, would he have time to read a letter?” “Certainly. Give it to me. I'll stay beside him and make sure he opens it.” Wang handed it over. “Then I rely on you. If the governor has any message, please come and let me know.” “Naturally. I understand.”

zh: “再托你一件事。”王有龄把靴页子里一大把红封套掏出来交给刘二，“节下的小意思，请你代为送一送。”这自是刘二乐于效劳的差使，喏喏连声地把王有龄送上了轿。等回到海运局，只见大门口越发热闹，挤满了陌不相识的人。看见大轿，都站了起来，注目致敬。王有龄端坐轿中，借一副墨镜遮掩，打量着那些人，一望便知，多数是来觅差使的，心内不免发愁，只怕粥少僧多，应酬不列，难免得罪人。果然，等他刚在签押房中坐定，门上立刻递进一大捧名帖和“八行”来，这就是做官的苦楚了，一个个要应付，看来头的大小，或者亲自接谈，或者请周委员等人代见，要想出许多力不从心的客气话来敷衍，这样忙到夕阳衔山，方始告一段落，这才想起刘二，何以未见有信息送来？等到上灯，依然音信杳然，王有龄有些沉不住气了！他照胡雪岩的话做，这天上午从藩司衙门回来，立即宣布，仍旧兼着海运局坐办的差使，希望发生“稳定军心”的作用，倘或事有变卦拆穿了西洋镜，传出去为人当笑话讲，这个面子可丢不起。正在这样嘀咕，胡雪岩来了。问知情形，也觉得事不可解，不过他信心未失，认为虽无好信息，但也没有坏消息，不必着急。
en: “One more favour.” Wang drew the handful of red envelopes from his boot and gave them to Liu. “A few small festival tokens. Please distribute them for me.” This was a duty Liu welcomed. With repeated assurances, he escorted Wang to his chair. Back at the bureau, the entrance was busier than ever, crowded with strangers. They rose respectfully at the sight of his chair. Sitting upright behind his dark spectacles, Wang examined them. Most were plainly seeking employment. He feared there were too many monks for too little porridge: he could not satisfy them all and would inevitably offend some. Sure enough, as soon as he sat down, a great bundle of cards and letters came in. Here was one of the hardships of office. Everyone had to be answered. Depending upon the importance of the connection, he received them personally or asked Zhou and others to do so. He had to devise countless polite phrases explaining what he could not do. Only when the sun touched the hills did the business briefly subside. Then he remembered Liu Er. Why had no message arrived? By lamplight there was still none, and Wang grew restless. Following Hu's advice, he had announced that morning, after returning from the treasury, that he would retain the bureau's directorship. He had hoped to steady the staff. If things changed and the pretence were exposed, the story would become a joke at his expense. He could not bear that loss of face. As he worried, Hu arrived. Hearing the situation, he too found it puzzling, but retained his confidence. There was no good news, but no bad news either. There was no need for alarm.

zh: “就算如此，刘二也该先来告诉我一声。”“这是刘二不知道你的用意，倘或他知道你这么着急，当然会先来说一声。”胡雪岩想了一下说，“雪公，你不妨先回府。一面止高升把刘二请了来问一问看，看黄抚台是怎么个表示？”“这话有理。就这么办！”高升这一去，又好半天没有信息。王有龄在家跟胡雪岩两个人对饮坐等，直等到钟打九下，才看见高升打着一盏灯笼把刘二照了进来。人已到了，王有龄便从容了，先问刘二吃过饭没有？刘二说是早已吃过，接着便说，“高二爷来的那一刻，我正在上头回公事，交代的事很多，所以耽误了。你老这封信，抚台早就看过，直到此刻才有话。”“噢！”王有龄见他慢条斯理地，十分着急，但急也只能急在心里，表面上一点不肯摆出来。“ 上头交代：请王大老爷到湖州接了印，一等有了头绪，赶快回省。这里的公事也很要紧！”“这里”当然是指海运局。王有龄喜心翻倒，与胡雪岩相视而笑，尽在不言。
en: “Even so, Liu should have told me something.” “He doesn't know why you're waiting. If he understood your anxiety, he'd certainly have come.” Hu thought a moment. “Go home first, and send Gao to invite him over. We can ask how the governor responded.” “That makes sense.” Gao too was gone a long time without word. Wang and Hu drank together at home while they waited. Not until the clock struck nine did Gao appear with a lantern, lighting Liu's way inside. Now that the man had arrived, Wang became composed and first asked whether he had eaten. Liu had eaten long before. “When Second Master Gao came, I was still reporting upstairs. There were many instructions, which delayed me. The governor read your letter early, but only now gave me a message.” “Oh?” Liu's unhurried manner made Wang impatient, though he would not show it. “His Excellency says: after His Honour Wang has received the seal at Huzhou and put things in order, he is to return promptly to the provincial capital. The business here is important too.” “Here” naturally meant the Sea Transport Bureau. Wang was overwhelmed with joy. He and Hu exchanged a smile that needed no words.

zh: 这下刘二才恍然大悟，心里懊悔，原来他海运局的差使，直到此刻，才算定局。早知如此，这个消息真是奇货可居，应当另有一番丑表功的说法。不过此刻也还不晚。于是他立即蹲下身子来请了个安：“恭喜王大老爷！我晓得你老急着等信息，伺候在我们大人身边，一步不敢离开，到底把好消息等到了。““承请之至。”王有龄懂他的意思，封了十两银子一个赏封，把刘二打发了走。
en: Only then did Liu understand. Wang's retention of the bureau had not been certain until this moment. He regretted his ignorance. Had he known, this news could have been made a valuable commodity, with a more elaborate account of his own services. But it was not too late. He immediately bent his knees in salute. “Congratulations, Your Honour! Knowing how anxiously you awaited news, I stayed beside our master without daring to move. At last I obtained the good word.” “I am most grateful.” Wang understood and sent him away with another envelope containing ten taels.

zh: “总算如愿以偿，各方面都可以交代了。”胡雪岩开玩笑他说，“王大老爷！我要讨桩差使，到湖州上任的船，由我替你去雇。”这自然是要照顾阿珠家的生意，王有龄使也笑道：“别的差使，无有不可，就是这桩不行。”两人哈哈大笑，把王太太惊动了，亲自出来探问，这是一个因头，其实她是要来听听消息，分享这一份她丈夫大交官运的喜悦，好在彼此已成通家至好，她也不避胡雪岩，坐在一起，向他谢了又谢，然后问道：“胡少爷，你怎么不捐个官？”“对了！”王有龄立即接口，“这实在是件要紧大事。雪岩，你有个功名在身上，办事要方便得多。譬如说海动局，你如果也是个州县州子，我就可以保你当委员，替我主持一切。事情不就好办了吗？”“话是不错。不过老实说，我现在顶要紧的一件事，是先要把阜康办了起来。”说着，向王太太看了一眼。王有龄会意，有些话他当着王太太不肯说，便托故把他妻子调了开去。“阜康要早早开张。藩台衙门那几万银子，得要快领下来做本钱。雪公，你明天再去催一催，我这里已经托了人了。”“这好办。”王有龄说，“我现在心里乱得很，不知道该先办何事，后办何事？”“官场的规矩我不十分在行。大家慢慢商量，尽这一夜工夫，理出个头绪来。一宵细谈，该办的事，孰先孰后，一条一条都写了下来。胡雪岩是忙着去筹备阜康，王有龄的第一件大事，是要去物色幕友。
en: “At last you've got what you wished, and everyone can be satisfied.” Hu joked, “Your Honour Wang, I have an assignment to request. Let me hire the boat for your journey to take office.” Naturally, this meant giving A'zhu's family the business. Wang laughed too. “Any other assignment is yours. Only that one is out of the question.” Their laughter drew Mrs Wang out to inquire. That was her excuse; she really wanted to hear the news and share the joy of her husband's rising fortune. They had become intimate family friends, so she no longer avoided Hu. Sitting with them, she thanked him repeatedly, then asked, “Young Master Hu, why don't you purchase an official title?” “Exactly!” Wang seized on it. “This is important. A qualification would make your work much easier. At the bureau, for instance, if you held a department or county magistrate's qualification, I could recommend you as a commissioner to oversee everything for me. Wouldn't that simplify matters?” “True. But my first concern is getting Fukang established.” Hu glanced at Mrs Wang. Understanding that some things could not be said before her, Wang found an excuse to send her away. “Fukang must open soon,” Hu continued. “We need those tens of thousands from the treasury as capital. Press them again tomorrow. I've already found someone to work on the matter below.” “That can be done. My mind is in such confusion that I don't know what to do first.” “I don't fully understand official practice. Let's discuss it patiently. We have the whole night to put things in order.” They talked through the night, writing down each task and its priority. Hu busied himself preparing Fukang. Wang's first major duty was to find private secretaries.

zh: 幕友的名堂甚多，刑、钱两席以外，还有管出纳的“帐房”、写信的“书启”，以及为子弟授书的“教读”、帮忙考试的“阅卷”、征收地了的“征比”等等。当然最重要的还是“刑名”和“钱谷”。臬司衙门的俞师爷，是早就答应过王有龄，为他好好物色的，所以第二夭他专诚去拜访俞师爷。来意不道自明，“刑名”一席，俞师爷已经替王有龄准备好了，就是他的学生。俞师爷的这个学生，名叫秦寿门，名为学生，其实年龄与俞师爷相差无几，当然也不是初出茅庐。大致走上幕宾这条路子，虽说“读书不成，去而学幕”，好象是末路，但却是“神仙、老虎、狗”的生涯。名幕的声光，十分煊赫，此辈不但律例烂熟，文笔畅达，而尤贵乎师承有自，见多识广，所以学幕的过程，十分重要。秦寿门跟随俞师爷多年，由州县开始，历经府、道，一直学到臬司衙门，了解地方上整套司法的程序，以及每一级的职权范围和特性，是谓“能得其全”，比那仅仅于州县，或是臬司衙门的，自然高明得多。他在十年前就已出道，馆地从来没有间断过，前年因为父母双亡，回到原籍绍兴奔丧，接着又生了一场病，最近身体复元来投靠老师，俞师爷正好把他荐给王有龄。当时请了来彼此见面，一谈之下，相当投机，王有龄心想，幕友除了自己来得以外，还要讲关系、通声气，否则本事虽大，事倍功半，现在是俞师爷介绍的人，将来不管什么案子，由县里申详到省，俞师爷当然要尽力维持，这就等于出一份“修金”，聘了两位幕友，岂不划算？
en: Private secretaries came in many varieties. Besides the legal and revenue advisers, there were accountants handling receipts and payments, correspondence secretaries, tutors for the official's children, examination assistants who read papers, collection specialists, and others. The legal and revenue posts were naturally the most important. Secretary Yu at the judicial commissioner's yamen had long promised to find suitable men, so Wang made a special call. His purpose needed no explanation. Yu had already chosen his own pupil for the legal post. This pupil, Qin Shoumen, was in fact nearly Yu's age and no novice. The profession was sometimes dismissed as a last resort for men who failed in their studies, but a secretary's life could be that of “an immortal, a tiger, or a dog.” Celebrated secretaries enjoyed great prestige. They needed not only command of statutes and precedents and a fluent pen, but sound professional lineage, broad knowledge, and experience. Their training was therefore crucial. Qin had followed Yu for years, beginning at county and department level, progressing through prefectural and circuit offices, and finally reaching the provincial judicial commission. He understood the entire local judicial process and the powers and characteristics of every level. This comprehensive experience made him superior to men trained only in a county office or only at the provincial commission. He had begun independent practice ten years earlier and had never lacked employment. Two years before, both parents died. He returned to Shaoxing for their funerals, then fell ill himself. Recently recovered, he had come to his teacher for assistance. Yu could now recommend him to Wang. They met and conversed agreeably. Wang reflected that, besides ability, secretaries needed connections and channels of communication; otherwise even great talent achieved little for the effort. Since Yu had introduced Qin, he would naturally support cases submitted from the county to the province. One salary would effectively secure two advisers. An excellent bargain.

zh: 于是即时下了口头聘约，彼此都很满意。王有龄对于另一位钱谷师爷，也是如法炮制，请藩署最出名的王师爷介绍，他介绍的是他的一个名叫杨用之的师兄弟，言明在先，人是勤恳老实，本事并不怎么样了不起。好在王有龄所重视的是借此拉上王师爷的关系，钱谷一道，他自己也懂得很多，幕友弱一些也不要紧。回到海运局，王有龄亲自动笔准备聘书，用大红全帖，面写“关书”二字，里面写的是：“敦聘寿门秦老夫子，在署理乌程县知县兼署湖州府知府任内，办理刑名事件，月奉修金纹银七十两，到馆起修。三节另奉贽敬纹银八两。谨订。”下面署款“教弟王有龄顿首拜。”不用官印、也不用私章，封入红封套内，加个签条，写的是“秦老夫子惠存”。杨用之的那份关书，款式也是一样，不过修金每月只有五十两，并且写明“不另致送节敬”，这是因为钱谷师爷，在每地丁钱粮征收完毕，另有好处的缘故。
en: They immediately agreed upon the engagement, to mutual satisfaction. Wang used the same method for the revenue post, asking the most celebrated Secretary Wang in the treasury to recommend someone. He proposed a fellow pupil, Yang Yongzhi, stating plainly that the man was diligent and honest rather than exceptionally able. That suited Wang, who chiefly wanted the connection with Secretary Wang. He himself knew much of revenue administration, so a less capable adviser would not matter. Back at the bureau, he personally prepared the letters of engagement on large red cards. The front bore the words “Letter of Engagement.” Inside Qin's, he wrote: “I respectfully engage Master Qin Shoumen to manage legal affairs during my tenure as acting magistrate of Wucheng County and acting prefect of Huzhou, at a monthly remuneration of seventy taels of standard silver, commencing upon arrival. A further ceremonial gift of eight taels will be offered at each of the three major festivals. This engagement is hereby confirmed.” He signed himself humbly as Wang Youling, bowing his head. Neither official nor private seal was used. The card went into a red envelope labelled “For Master Qin's keeping.” Yang's letter followed the same form, but offered fifty taels a month and expressly excluded additional festival gifts, since a revenue secretary received other benefits after each collection of land and grain taxes.

zh: 等把关书送了去，王有龄随即又下帖子请客。幕友虽无官职，但地位与他的“东翁”相同，尤其是刑钱两席，有一定的称呼，州县称“大老爷”，所以秦寿门和杨用之，都该称为“师大老爷”。两位“师大老爷”是分开来请的，因为幕友最讲究札数，他们在衙里自成夭地，长官有事，要移樽就教。初一、十五就象衙参那样，要恭具衣冠去拜访问好。岁时佳节，特为设宴奉请，平时请客一定要请幕友坐首座，否则就不必奉邀。现在虽还未到馆，已要按规矩办事，怕秦、杨二人，哪个坐首座，哪个坐次席，难于安排，所以索性分开来请，两个都是首座。陪客自然是胡雪岩和周、吴两委员。第一天请的是刑名师爷秦寿门，帖子发了出去，这位贵宾专函辞射，理由是他吃长素，不便叨拢。这也好办，杭州四大丛林的素斋，无不精致万分，雷峰塔下的净慈寺，方丈心悟是王有龄的同乡，素有往还，更加方便，于是另外备了个“洁治素斋候光”的请柬送出去。秦寿门复信，欣然应诺。到了那天轿子出清彼门，中“柳浪闻莺”下船，先逛西湖，后吃素斋。净慈的方丈心悟以半主半客的身分作陪，席间问起秦寿门吃长素的原因，他回答得很坦率。
en: After sending the letters, Wang issued dinner invitations. Though they held no official rank, private secretaries enjoyed standing equal to that of their employer. The legal and revenue advisers in particular had a prescribed form of address: since a local magistrate was called “His Honour,” they were accorded the corresponding honour as secretarial masters. They were invited separately. Secretaries insisted upon ceremony, maintaining a domain of their own within the yamen. An official seeking advice went to them. On the first and fifteenth of each month he dressed formally to pay his respects, much as at an official audience. Special banquets were offered on festivals. At ordinary dinners a secretary must occupy the seat of honour or not be invited at all. Although the two had not yet joined him, Wang must already follow the rules. To avoid deciding which should sit first and which second, he entertained them separately, giving each the first seat. Hu, Zhou, and Wu would accompany him. Qin was invited first, but declined by letter because he observed a strict vegetarian diet and did not wish to cause trouble. This was easily remedied. The vegetarian food of Hangzhou's four great monasteries was exquisite. At Jingci Monastery beneath Leifeng Pagoda, the abbot Xinwu was Wang's fellow townsman and an old acquaintance. Wang sent a new invitation promising a carefully prepared vegetarian meal, which Qin gladly accepted. On the appointed day, their chairs left through Qingbo Gate. They boarded a boat at “Listening to Orioles among the Willows,” toured West Lake, and then ate. Abbot Xinwu joined them as half host, half guest. Asked why he had become a lifelong vegetarian, Qin answered frankly.

zh: “ 有老和尚在，不敢打诳语，我是忏悔宿业。”寿门说，“前两年我在顺天府衙门‘作客，办一件案子，误信人言，以致’失出‘，虽无责任，此心耿耿不安，不久，先父先母，双刃弃世，我辞馆回乡，料理完了丧事，自己又是一场大病，九死一生。病中忏悔，倘能不死，从此长焉念佛，一点诚心，固然蒙菩萨鉴怜，一天好一天，如今是我还愿的时候。”“诚则灵！”心悟不断点头，“种爪得瓜，种豆得豆，因果不可不信。”“我本想从此封笔，无奈家累甚重，不得不重作冯妇。公门之中，容易作孽，多蒙东翁台爱，我别无所报，为东翁种些福田。”“是，是！”王有龄很诚恳地答道，“我所望于老夫子的，也就是如此。”“公门之中也好修行。”胡雪岩安慰他说，“秦老夫子无心中积的德，一定不少。”“这自然也有。我们这一行，多少年来师弟相传的心法：”救生不救死‘。就是体上天好生之德。然而说句老实话，也是‘乐’在其中。“这名话很含蓄，但在座的人无不明白，救了‘生’才有红色收入，一味替死者伸冤，除了苦主，谁来见情？“话又说回来。干我们这一行，到底积德的多，造孽的少，不比刑官狱吏，造孽容易积德难。”
en: “With the abbot present, I dare not speak falsely. I am repenting past wrongdoing. A few years ago, while employed at the Shuntian prefectural yamen, I mistakenly trusted someone's account and allowed a guilty man to escape his proper punishment. Although I bore no formal responsibility, my conscience remained troubled. Soon afterwards both my parents died. I resigned, returned home, and arranged their funerals, then fell dangerously ill myself. During the illness I repented and vowed that, if I survived, I would henceforth abstain from meat and recite Buddhist prayers. The bodhisattva evidently took pity on my sincerity. I improved day by day. Now I am fulfilling that vow.” “Sincerity brings a response,” Xinwu said, nodding repeatedly. “Plant melons and you reap melons; plant beans and you reap beans. Cause and consequence cannot be disregarded.” “I intended to lay down my pen altogether, but my family obligations are heavy, and I have had to return to the profession. It is easy to do wrong in public office. I have nothing with which to repay my employer's kindness except to cultivate some merit on his behalf.” “Indeed,” Wang answered earnestly. “That is exactly what I hope for.” “One can also cultivate virtue in public service,” Hu reassured him. “You must have done much good without realising it.” “Naturally, there has been some. Our professional rule, passed from master to pupil for years, is ‘Save the living, not the dead,’ in accordance with Heaven's love of life. Though, frankly, there are rewards in that too.” The words were discreet, but everyone understood. Saving the living brought monetary gifts. If one merely sought justice for the dead, who but the bereaved would show gratitude? “Still, our profession does more good than harm. It differs from prison officials and jailers, for whom wrongdoing is easy and merit difficult.”

zh: “这又是为什么呢？”胡雪岩很感兴味地问。“ 此无他，到底自己可以作主？譬如象雪公这样的东家，自然不许我们造孽，即使所遇非人，我们只要自己把握得定，东家也不能强人所难。狱里就不同了，真正是晴无天日！”“怎么呢？”“一句话，非钱不行，没有钱，那地方比猪圈都不如，有钱的，跟自己家里一样，不但起居饮食舒服，甚至妻妾要以进去伴宿。”“我也听说过。”王有龄问道，“真有这样的事？”“当然有！我说个故事为诸公下酒，就出在我们浙江，那是道光年间的事……”
en: “Why is that?” Hu asked with interest. “Simply because we can ultimately decide for ourselves. An employer like Mr Xuexuan would naturally forbid wrongdoing. Even under the wrong man, if we hold firm, he cannot force us against our principles. Prison is different. There truly is no daylight there.” “How so?” “In a word, nothing happens without money. Without it, the place is worse than a pigsty. With it, one lives as comfortably as at home. Food and lodging are excellent, and even wives or concubines can come in to spend the night.” “I've heard that too,” Wang said. “Does it really happen?” “Certainly. Let me tell you a story to accompany your wine. It happened here in Zhejiang, during the Daoguang reign.”

zh: 据说，道光年培有个富家子弟，犯了命案，情节甚重。由县、府、道，一直到省里，都维持“斩立决”的罪名，只待刑部公文下来，便要处决。这个富家子弟是三世单传，所以他家上下打点，只想救出一条命来。无奈情真罪实，遇着的又都是清官，以致钱虽花得不少，毫无作用，只都便宜了中间经手的人。那富家翁眼睁睁看着要绝后，百万家财，身后将为五服以外的族人所瓜分，无论如何于心不甘。于是经人指点，备了一份重礼去请教一个以善于出奇计，外号“鬼见愁”的刑名师爷，不得已而求于次，只想他的在狱中的儿子，能够留下一点骨血，哪怕是个女孩子也好，问那刑名师爷，可有办法？办法是有，但不能包养儿子，因为这是任何人所无能为力的。但就照“鬼见愁”的办法，已能令人满意。他答应可以让那富家子，多活三个月，在这三个月中，以重金觅得数名且男的健妇，送到狱中为富家子荐寝。当然，狱中是早已打点好的出入无阻，每天黎明有人在监狱后门迎接，接着健妇送到家供养。事先已讲明白，要在他家住几个月，若无喜信，送一笔钱放回，有了喜信就一直住下去，直到分娩为止，那时或去或留，另有协议。
en: A young man from a rich family had committed a serious homicide. County, prefectural, circuit, and provincial authorities all upheld immediate execution by beheading. Only the Board of Punishments' authorisation remained before the sentence could be carried out. He was the family's sole male heir for three generations. They spent money on every possible approach in the hope of saving him. But the facts were clear and the officials honest. Their considerable expenditure benefited only the intermediaries. His father could not bear to see the line end and his enormous fortune eventually divided among distant clansmen beyond the prescribed degrees of mourning. On someone's advice, he took a substantial gift to a legal secretary renowned for ingenious schemes, nicknamed “the Man Even Ghosts Fear.” Unable to save his son, he asked for the next best thing: could the prisoner leave a child, even a girl? There was a method, though naturally nobody could guarantee a son. The secretary promised three more months of life. During that time, several healthy women considered likely to bear sons would be paid generously to visit the prisoner. The jailers had already been bribed, so access was unrestricted. Each dawn someone would meet the women at the back gate and take them to the wealthy household, where they were maintained. It was agreed beforehand that they would stay several months. Those who did not conceive would receive money and leave; those who did would remain until the birth, with further arrangements made afterwards.

zh: 这样过了十几天，刑部的复文到了，是“钉封文书”，一望便知是核准了“斩立决”。“慢来，慢来！”胡雪岩打断秦寿门的话问道：“不是说可以活三个月？何以前后一个月不到？““少安毋躁，”秦寿门笑道，“当然另有道理，不然何以鬼见了都愁？”他接着又讲……
en: Yet after only a dozen days, the ministry's reply arrived in a cord-fastened sealed dispatch. One glance showed that it authorised immediate execution. “Wait!” Hu interrupted. “Didn't you say he had three months? It hasn't even been one.” “Be patient.” Qin smiled. “There is naturally another explanation. Otherwise, why would even ghosts fear the man?” He continued the story.

zh: 既称“斩立决”，等“钉封文书”一到，就得“出红差”，知县升堂，传齐三班六房和刽子手，把犯人从监狱里提了出来，当堂开拆文书。打开来一看，知县愣住了，封套上的姓名不错，里面的文书，完全不对，姓名不对，案情不对，地方也不对，应该发到贵州的，发到浙江来了。没有核准斩立决的文书，如何可以杀人？犯人依旧送回监狱，文书退了回去。杭州到京师，再慢也不过二十天，但是要等贵州把那弄错了的文书送回刑部，“云贵半爿天”，一来一往就三个月都不止，便宜了贵州的那犯人，平白多活了几个月。“这不用说，当然是在部里做了手脚？”王有龄问。“是的。”秦寿门答道，“运动了一个刑部主事。这算是疏忽，罚俸三个月，不过几十两银子，但就这样一举手之劳的‘疏忽’，非一千银子不办。”“这是好事！为人延嗣，绝大阴功，还有一千两银子进帐。”胡雪岩笑道：“何乐不为？”
en: An immediate-execution order required the execution party to be assembled as soon as the sealed dispatch arrived. The magistrate took his seat, summoned the yamen personnel and executioner, and had the prisoner brought from jail. He opened the dispatch in court—and froze. The name on the cover was correct, but everything inside was wrong: the name, the case, the place. A document meant for Guizhou had reached Zhejiang. Without proper authorisation, how could he execute the man? The prisoner returned to jail and the document was sent back. Even a slow journey from Hangzhou to the capital took no more than twenty days, but the ministry had to wait for Guizhou to return the other misdirected document. Yunnan and Guizhou seemed half a world away. The round trip would take more than three months. The prisoner there benefited too, unexpectedly gaining several months of life. “Naturally, someone at the ministry had arranged it?” Wang asked. “Yes. A secretary at the Board of Punishments was persuaded. It counted as negligence, punishable by three months' salary—only a few dozen taels. But this effortless act of ‘negligence’ cost a thousand taels to arrange.” “A good deed!” Hu laughed. “To preserve a family line is great hidden merit, and brings a thousand taels besides. Why not do it?”

zh: “其奈坏法何？”秦寿门说，“倘或查封、抄家的文书，也是这么横生枝节，国库的损失，谁来认赔？”“若有其事，也算疏忽？”“此是何等大事，不容疏忽也不会疏忽。国法不外乎人情，所以听讼执法，只从人情上去揣摩，疑窦立见。譬如说某人向来精细，而某事忽然疏忽，此一疏忽又有大出入，其事便可疑了。又譬如‘例案’，向来如此办理，而主管其事的忽然说，这么办是冤枉的，驳了下来，甚至已定谳的案子，把它翻案。试问，这一案冤枉，以前同样的案子就不冤枉？何以不翻？只从这上面去细想一想，其中出了什么鬼？不言可知。”听这番话，足见得秦寿门是个极明白事理的人。王有龄当然觉得欣慰。
en: “But what of the damage to the law?” Qin asked. “If orders for sealing property or confiscating an estate suffered similar complications, who would compensate the treasury?” “Would that count as negligence too?” “Such important matters admit no negligence, nor would it occur by accident. Law cannot be separated from human motives. When hearing cases and enforcing it, examine those motives and the doubts become apparent. Suppose a habitually meticulous man suddenly makes a mistake, and the mistake makes an enormous difference. That is suspicious. Or take a class of cases always decided one way. Suddenly the responsible official declares that practice unjust, rejects it, or even overturns a final judgement. If this case was unjust, were the earlier identical cases not unjust too? Why not reverse them? Consider that carefully, and the hidden interference becomes obvious.” These remarks showed Qin's clear understanding of affairs. Wang was naturally pleased.

zh: 但刑名一道对县官的前程，关系太大，老百姓对父母官的信服与否，首先也就是从刑名上看。只要年成好，地方富庶，钱粮的浮收及各种摊派，稍微过分些，都还能容忍，若是审理官司，有理的一方受屈，无理的一方赢了，即或是无心之失，也会招致老百生极大的不满，说起来必是“贪赃枉法”。所以王有龄对秦寿门看得比杨用之重，事先跟胡雪岩说好了的，自己不便频频质疑，要他借闲谈多发问，借以考一考秦寿门的本事，此时便又递了个眼色过去。于是胡雪岩装得似懂非懂的样子，用好奇而仰慕的语气问道，“都说刑名老夫子一支笔厉害，一个字的出入，就是一家人的祸福，又说‘天下文章在幕府’，我问过人，也就不出个所以然。今天遇见秦老夫子，一定可以教一教我了！”又捧刑名师爷又捧他本人，这顶双料的高帽子，秦寿门戴得很舒服，致且酒到半酣，谈兴正好，便矜持地笑道：“读书万卷不读律，致君尧舜知何术？‘所谓’天下文章，出于幕府‘，言其实用而已，至于一个字的出入，关乎一家人祸福，这话倒也不假。不过，舞文弄墨，我辈大忌。总之，无事不可生事，有事不可怕事。”在座的人连连点头，吴委员肚千里有些墨水，尤其觉得“舞文弄墨，我辈大忌”八个字，近乎见道之言，因而说道。“我也要请教！”“先说无事不可生事……”
en: But legal affairs mattered enormously to a magistrate's career. They were also the first basis upon which the people judged their parent-official. With good harvests and a prosperous district, they might tolerate somewhat excessive additions to taxes and miscellaneous levies. If the rightful party lost a lawsuit and the wrongdoer won, however, even an innocent mistake would provoke deep resentment and accusations of corruption and injustice. Wang therefore valued Qin more highly than Yang. He had agreed with Hu beforehand that, since he could not repeatedly question his new adviser himself, Hu should test him through conversation. He now gave another signal. Hu adopted an expression of partial understanding and asked with curious admiration, “Everyone says a legal master's pen is formidable: one altered character can determine a family's fortune. They also say the finest writing comes from secretaries' offices. I've asked about it without receiving a clear explanation. Today you can surely enlighten me.” This double compliment, to his profession and himself, pleased Qin. Half warmed by wine and enjoying the discussion, he smiled with restrained pride. “‘Read ten thousand volumes but neglect the law—how will you guide your sovereign to the virtue of Yao and Shun?’ The claim about writing refers to its practical use. As for a single character determining a family's fortune, that is true. But manipulating words is our profession's great taboo. In short: where no trouble exists, don't create it; where trouble arises, don't fear it.” Everyone nodded. Wu, who had some literary education, particularly admired the warning against manipulating words and asked for an explanation. “First, not creating trouble where none exists...” Qin began.

zh: 秦寿门讲了个故事作例证：曾有一省的巡抚与藩司不和，巡抚必欲去之而后快，苦于那藩司既清廉又能干，找不着他的错处。后来找到一个机会，文庙丁祭，那藩司正好重伤风，行札的时候，咳个不停，巡抚抓住他这个错，跟幕友商量，那幕友顺从东家的意思，舞文弄墨，大张旗鼓，奏劾那藩司失仪不敬。凡有弹劾，朝廷通常总要查了再说，情节重大则由京里特派钦差，驰驿查办。类此事件，往往交“将军”或者“学政”查报。那一省没有驻防的将军，但学政是每一省都有的，这位学政文庙丁祭也在场，知道藩司的失仪，情非得已。就算真的失仪，至多事后教训一顿，又何至于毛举细故，专折参劾？由于这一份不满的心情，那学政不但要帮藩司的忙，还要给巡抚吃点苦头。但是他不便公然指摘巡抚，让朝延疑心他有意袒护藩司，所以措词甚难。这位学政未曾中举成进士以前，原学过刑名，想了半天，从巡抚原奏的“亲见”二字中，欣然有悟，随即提笔复奏，他说他丁祭那天，虽也在场，但无法复查这一案，因为他“位列前班，理无后顾”，不知道藩司失仪了没有？就这轻描淡写八个字，军机大臣一看便知道，是巡抚有意找藩司的麻烦，因为行礼时巡抚也是跪在藩司前面，如何知道后面的藩司失仪？照此说来，是巡抚抚失仪往后面看了，才发现藩司失仪。结果两个人都有处分。原被告各打五十板，自然是原告失面子，被告虽受罚，心里是痛快的。
en: He gave an example. A governor disliked his provincial treasurer and wanted him removed. Unfortunately, the treasurer was both honest and capable, leaving no fault to seize upon. At last an opportunity came. During a sacrifice at the Confucian temple, the treasurer had a severe cold and coughed continually through the ceremony. The governor discussed this lapse with his secretary. Obeying his employer's wishes, the secretary used elaborate wording to make a great affair of it, impeaching the treasurer for ceremonial misconduct and disrespect. The court usually investigated before acting upon an accusation. Grave cases brought a special commissioner from the capital by express relay. Matters of this kind were often referred to the garrison general or provincial education commissioner. That province had no resident garrison general, but every province had an education commissioner. He too had attended the sacrifice and knew that the treasurer's conduct was involuntary. Even if it amounted to a breach of decorum, a reprimand afterwards should have sufficed. Why magnify a trifle into a special memorial of impeachment? Resenting this, he wanted not only to help the treasurer but to make the governor suffer. Yet an open criticism might lead the court to suspect partiality, making the wording difficult. Before passing the provincial and metropolitan examinations, the education commissioner had trained in legal work. After much thought, he found inspiration in the governor's claim to have “personally witnessed” the offence. His reply said that, although present, he could not verify it: “My place was in the forward rank; propriety forbade looking behind.” Those unobtrusive words made the matter plain to the Grand Councillors. The governor too had knelt ahead of the treasurer. How could he have seen misconduct behind him? He must himself have broken decorum by turning round. Both officials were punished. With plaintiff and defendant treated alike, the plaintiff lost face, while the defendant, though punished, felt satisfied.

zh: “这真是‘世不本无事，庸人自扰之’。”吴委员说，“坏在那巡抚的幕友不能痛切规劝。”“这话说中的症结所在。”秦寿门向王有龄看了一眼，“我辈既蒙东家不弃，处事自有必不可摇的宗旨，一时依从，留下后患，自误误人，千万不可。只是忠言往往逆耳，难碍有几位东家没有脾气。”“老大子请放心！”王有龄急忙表明态度，“我奉托了老替子，将来刑名方面，自然都请老夫子作主。”“有东翁这句话，我可以放心放手了。今天我借花献佛，先告个罪，将来要请东翁恕我专擅之罪。”说着他举杯相敬，王有龄欣然接受，宾主如鱼得水，在座的人亦都觉得很愉快。轰然祝饮，闹过一阵，重拾中断的话题。
en: “Truly, there was no trouble until a foolish man made it,” Wu said. “The fault lay in the governor's secretary failing to remonstrate firmly.” “You've identified the essential point.” Qin glanced at Wang. “Once an employer has honoured us with his trust, we must hold to unshakable principles. Compliance for a moment that leaves trouble for the future harms both him and us. It must never happen. Unfortunately, loyal advice often jars upon the ear, and few employers have no temper.” “Rest assured,” Wang promptly declared. “Having entrusted the post to you, I shall naturally leave legal affairs to your judgement.” “With that assurance, I can act confidently. Taking advantage of this hospitality, let me apologise in advance and ask you to forgive any future appearance of overstepping my authority.” He raised his cup. Wang gladly accepted the toast. Host and guest were perfectly at ease, and everyone shared their pleasure. After a noisy round of drinking, they returned to the interrupted subject.

zh: “现在要谈有事不可怕事。”吴委员提高了声音说道，“索性也请老夫子举例以明之。”秦寿门略略沉吟了一下说“有事不可怕事者，是要沉得住气，气稳则心定，心定则神闲，死棋肚里才会出仙着。大致古今律法，不论如何细密，总有漏洞，事理也是一样，有时道理不通，大家习焉不察，也就过去了，而看来不可思议之事，细想一想竟是道理极通，无可驳诘。所以只要心定神闲，想得广、想得透，蹈瑕乘隙，避重就轻，大事化小，小事化无，亦并不难。刚才提到‘ 钉封文书’，我就说个钉封文书的妙事。在座各位，“他看着王有龄问道，”想来东翁一定见过这玩意？““见过。”王有龄答道，“原来钉封文书，用意在示机密，亦不光是州县处决犯人非受领钉封文书不可，访拿要犯也用钉封文书。久而久之，成为具文，封套上钉个‘瓣’，用细麻绳一拴，人人可以拆开来看，最机密变成最不机密，真正是始料所不及！”“一点都不错。这件妙事，毛病就出在‘人人可以拆开来看’上面。钉封文书按驿站走，每经一县，都要加盖大印。公事过手，遇着好事的县大爷，就拆开来看一看依旧封好。有这么一位县太爷，鸦片大瘾，每天晚上在签押房里，躺在烟铺上看公事。这天也是拆了一封钉封文书看，迷迷糊糊，把那通文书在烟灯上饶掉了，”
en: “Now for not fearing trouble when it comes,” Wu said loudly. “Please give us an example of that too.” Qin considered briefly. “It means keeping one's composure. A steady temper settles the mind; a settled mind allows clear thought. Then an apparently lost position may yield an inspired move. However detailed the law, ancient or modern, there are always gaps. Reasoning is similar. Sometimes an argument is unsound, but familiarity keeps everyone from noticing. Something apparently inconceivable may, on examination, prove entirely reasonable and beyond refutation. With composure, breadth, and depth of thought, one can find the opening, avoid the heavier consequence, and turn a great problem into a small one, then into none. Since we mentioned cord-fastened dispatches, let me tell you an ingenious story about one. I suppose my employer has seen them?” “Yes,” Wang replied. “Originally their fastening signified confidentiality. They were used not only for execution orders but for arresting important criminals. In time the practice became a formality: a flap fixed to the cover, tied with thin hemp cord. Anyone could open it. The most confidential document became the least secure—an outcome surely never intended.” “Exactly. This story turns upon that freedom to open them. Such dispatches travelled by post relay. Each county through which they passed added its official seal. An inquisitive magistrate handling one might open it, read it, and tie it up again. One such magistrate was a heavy opium smoker. Every evening he read official papers while reclining beside his pipe. One night, half dazed, he opened a dispatch and accidentally burned its contents over the opium lamp.”

zh: 这一下，那县太爷才惊醒过来，烧掉了钉封文书，是件不得了的事！急忙移樽就教，到刑名师爷那里求援。“封套在不在？”那刑名师爷问。“封套还在。”“那不要紧！请东翁交了给我。顺便带大印来。”县太爷照办不误，等封套取到，那刑名师爷取张白纸折好，往里一塞，拴好麻绳，盖上大印，交了回去。“交驿递发下一站！”“老夫子，”县太爷迟疑地问道：“这行吗？下一站发觉了怎么办？”“东家，请你自己去想。”那刑名师爷说，“换了你是下一县，打开来一看，里头是张白纸，请问你怎么办？”秦寿门把那个故事讲到此处，不需再往下说，在座的人应都明白，显然的，有人发现了是张白纸，也不敢声张，更不敢多事退回去。因为倘或如此，便先犯了窃视机密文书的过失，这与那学政的“位列前班，理无后顾”八字，有异曲同功之妙。
en: That brought him sharply to his senses. Destroying a confidential dispatch was an appalling offence. He hurried to seek his legal secretary's help. “Do you still have the cover?” “Yes.” “Then don't worry. Give it to me, and bring the official seal.” The magistrate obeyed. The secretary folded a blank sheet, put it inside, tied the cord, stamped the seal, and handed it back. “Send it by relay to the next station.” “Will that do?” the magistrate asked hesitantly. “What if the next station discovers it?” “Think for yourself. Suppose you're the next magistrate. You open it and find a blank sheet. What would you do?” Qin needed to go no further. Everyone understood. Anyone finding the blank page would dare neither announce the discovery nor return it and cause trouble: that would first expose his own offence of opening a confidential document. The reasoning resembled the education commissioner's statement that his forward position forbade looking behind.

zh: “刑名虽是‘法家’，也要多读老庄之书，才能有些妙悟。”王有龄感叹着说，“人不能有所蔽，有所蔽则能见秋毫，不见舆薪。世上明明有许多极浅显的道理，偏偏有人看不破，这是哪里说起？”这番议论一发，便把话题引了开去。闲谈到夕阳衔山，方始散席，依旧荡桨回城。第二请钱谷师爷杨用之，在西湖里的一条画舫上设席，陪客依旧是胡雪岩和周、吴两委员。由于阜康钱庄创设以后，预计是要用湖州府和乌程县解省的公款，作为资本，这与钱谷师爷有密切的关系，因此胡雪岩对杨用之，特别笼络。杨用之赋性忠厚老实，是最容易对付的人，以胡雪岩的手腕，把他摆布得服服帖帖，颇有相见恨晚之感。其实胡雪岩的手腕也很简单，凡是忠厚老实的人，都喜欢别人向他请教，而他自己亦往往知无不言，言无不尽。胡雪岩会说话，更会听话，不管那人是如何地语言无味，他能一本正经，两眼注视，仿佛听得极感兴味似地，同时，他也真的是在听，紧要关头补充一两语。引申一两义，使得滔滔不绝者，有莫逆于心之快，自然觉得投机而成至交。
en: “Though legal advisers belong to the school of law, they should also read Laozi and Zhuangzi to gain such insights,” Wang reflected. “A man must not allow his vision to be obstructed, seeing an autumn hair but missing a cartload of firewood. There are so many obvious truths that people nevertheless fail to see. How can one explain it?” The discussion moved to other matters. They talked until sunset, then left the table and rowed back to the city. The following day, Wang entertained the revenue secretary Yang Yongzhi aboard a pleasure boat on West Lake, again accompanied by Hu, Zhou, and Wu. Fukang was expected to use Huzhou Prefecture's and Wucheng County's public remittances to the provincial treasury as capital. Since the revenue secretary was closely involved, Hu made a special effort to cultivate him. Yang was straightforward and honest, and therefore easy to manage. Hu soon made him wholly accommodating, with the feeling that they should have met long before. In fact, the method was simple. Straightforward men liked to be consulted and generally shared all they knew. Hu spoke well, but listened still better. However dull another man's words, he could attend gravely, eyes fixed upon him, as though fascinated. He really did listen, adding a remark or developing a point at the crucial moment. The speaker then felt deeply understood, and congenial conversation became close friendship.

zh: 杨用之的本事不怎么好，但以他的性格随和，所以交游甚广，加以遇着胡雪岩，不知不觉地提起了谈兴，讲了许多时人的轶闻，最后谈到湖州府的人物，他提起一个人叫钱江，问王有龄认不认识？“我听说过他，是湖州府长兴县人，曾跟我们福建的林文忠公，一起遣戍伊犁，由此出名。听说他是个奇士。想来林文忠公所赏识的人物，总不会错的。”王有龄问道：“怎么老夫子忽然提到这个人，莫非有他的新闻？”“也好说是新闻。不过这条新闻，与各州县利害关系甚大，还不知道朝廷的主张如何？”“喔，要请教。”“这要从一位达官谈起，雷以諴其人，东翁总知道？”“知道。”王有龄说，“此公湖北人，以左副御史会同河道总督巡视黄河口岸。前些日子看邸抄，说他自请讨贼，现在募了一万人，驻军江北高邮，扼守扬州东南，很打了几场胜仗。”“是的，钱江就在他幕府里。”杨用之说，“有兵无饷，仗是打不下去的，朝廷的宗旨，反正只要你能募兵筹饷，自己去想办法，无不赞成的。听说钱江现在为雷军划一策，在水陆要冲，设局设卡，凡行商经过，看他所带货物，估价抽税，大致千取其一，称为‘厘捐’，除了行商，当地店铺亦照此抽税。收入颇为可观，听说各省都有仿照的意思。只是此法病商，朝廷或者不许。”
en: Yang was not exceptionally able, but his agreeable temperament had given him many acquaintances. Hu's company drew him into an animated account of contemporary figures. Eventually, discussing Huzhou, he mentioned Qian Jiang and asked whether Wang knew him. “I've heard of him. He comes from Changxing County in Huzhou Prefecture. He became known through being exiled to Ili with our Fujian statesman Lin Wenzhong. They say he's an extraordinary man. Someone appreciated by Lord Lin can't be ordinary. Why do you mention him? Is there news?” “You could call it news. But it affects local officials profoundly, and we don't yet know the court's view.” “Please explain.” “We must begin with a senior official. You know Lei Yixian?” “Yes. A Hubei man. As senior vice censor-in-chief, he joined the Director-General of River Conservancy to inspect the Yellow River's outlet. Recently I read that he volunteered to fight the rebels. He has recruited ten thousand men, stationed them at Gaoyou north of the Yangtze, and is guarding the southeastern approach to Yangzhou. He's won several battles.” “Exactly. Qian Jiang serves on his staff. Troops without pay cannot fight. The court's position is that anyone able to recruit men and raise funds should devise his own means, and it will approve. I hear Qian has proposed collection offices and checkpoints at important land and water routes. Travelling merchants are assessed on the value of their goods, generally one part in a thousand. The levy is called lijin. Local shops pay on the same basis. The receipts are considerable, and other provinces are reportedly considering imitation. But since it harms trade, the court may refuse it.”

zh: 杨用之所谈的新闻，以及认为在创议中的“厘捐”会“病商”的见解，恰好给了王有龄一个机会，聘用刑、钱两幕友，他跟胡雪岩曾仔细谈过，刑名是外行，非倚托秦寿门不可，所以先要考一考他的本事。钱谷则王有龄自己就很精通，但幕友的传统，向来独立办事，不喜东家干涉，平和的还表面上有所敷衍，专断的根本就置之不理，所以胡雪岩设计，由他自己用感情来笼络杨用之，而王有龄则要拿点本事给他看看，这样双管齐下，让杨用之怀德畏威，把他收服，才能指挥如意。所以王有龄听了他的话，觉得不妨趁些机会，展示所学。“ ‘病商’恐未必！”他一开口就是辩驳语气，“本朝的赋税制度，异于前代，一遇用兵之时，必须另筹军费，以我看，开办‘厘捐’，比较起来，还不失为利多害少的好办法。”这笼统一句话，是做文章的一个“帽子”，王有龄既有炫耀之意，便得从头讲起。自古以来，国家岁收的主要项目，就是地了与钱粮，明朗未年不断“加派”，搞得民不聊生，庄稼人苦得要死，到最后只好弃地而逃，此为“流寇”猖獗，终以亡明的一大关键。
en: This news, and Yang's view that the proposed lijin would harm merchants, gave Wang his opportunity. He and Hu had discussed the two secretaries carefully. Law was outside Wang's expertise, so he must rely upon Qin and first test his ability. Revenue administration was different: Wang understood it well. Yet secretaries traditionally worked independently and disliked interference. An accommodating one might give an outwardly polite response; an autocratic one would simply ignore his employer. Hu's plan was therefore to win Yang's affection while Wang demonstrated enough knowledge to command respect. With gratitude and apprehension working together, Yang could be brought under effective direction. Wang seized the moment to display his learning. “I'm not sure it necessarily harms trade,” he began in an argumentative tone. “Our dynasty's tax system differs from those of earlier times. Whenever war comes, military funds must be raised separately. Comparatively speaking, lijin may still offer more benefit than harm.” This broad proposition served as the introduction to an essay. Intent upon demonstrating his knowledge, Wang began at the beginning. From ancient times, the chief annual revenues had been land and poll taxes and grain levies. Repeated additional assessments late in the Ming had made life intolerable. Farmers suffered so greatly that they abandoned their fields and fled. This was a major cause of the spread of roaming rebels and, ultimately, the dynasty's fall.

zh: 清兵入关，到圣祖平定三藩之乱，始得奠定国基。鉴于前朝之失，颁发“永不加赋”的诏令，此为清朝的一大仁政，亦为满族得以长主中原的一大凭借。后世诸帝，对圣祖的这个诏谕，信守不坠。此外国家岁收，还有关税、盐课两项，但地丁占岁收总额的三分之二，既有永不加赋的限制，则岁收就有了定额。风调雨顺、刀兵不起的太平岁月，固然可以支应，但一遇用兵，额外的军费负担，即无着落，倘或水旱年荒，一面要减免丁漕，一面要办赈济，收入减少，支出增加，又如何应付？再如刀兵水旱一齐来，火上加油，两面发烧，更是件不得了的事。
en: After the Qing entered China, the Kangxi emperor's suppression of the Three Feudatories finally secured the dynasty's foundations. Taking warning from the Ming, he issued an edict promising never to increase taxation. This was one of the dynasty's great benevolent measures and a principal reason the Manchus could long rule the central plains. Later emperors faithfully maintained it. Customs and salt duties also supplied annual revenue, but land and poll taxes represented two-thirds of the total. With an undertaking never to increase them, annual receipts were effectively fixed. They could cover expenditure in peaceful years of favourable weather. But war brought extra military costs with no provision. Drought or flood required both tax remissions and famine relief: income fell while expenditure rose. How could that be managed? If war and natural disaster coincided, both sides of the crisis intensified.

zh: “这有两个办法弥补，一靠平时蓄积。”王有龄从容议论：“虽然天子富有四海，国家收入与宫廷收入，还是有区分的。这个制度从汉朝就很完备了，‘大司农’掌国家度支，‘少府’管天子的私财。私财有余，国币不足，国家必乱。宋太祖平服十国，所得金银珍宝虽输于内府，但另行封存，称为‘封桩银’。他的打算是积到相当数目，要把‘燕云十六州’买回来。可惜徽宗不肖，以内府所积，用来起‘民岳’，才有金兵入寇之事。前明更不必说，户部穷得要命，宫内蓄积如山，到最后，白白便宜了‘流寇’。本朝就不同了，蓄只于国库而非内务府。”
en: “There are two ways to meet the shortfall,” Wang continued calmly. “The first is savings accumulated in ordinary times. Though the emperor possesses all within the four seas, state revenue and palace revenue are separate. The distinction was already well developed under the Han: the Grand Minister of Agriculture managed public expenditure, while the Privy Treasurer managed the sovereign's private wealth. If the ruler has a surplus while the state lacks funds, disorder follows. When the founding Song emperor subdued the Ten Kingdoms, their gold, silver, and jewels went into the palace treasury, but were separately sealed as a special reserve. He intended to accumulate enough to buy back the Sixteen Prefectures of Yan and Yun. Unfortunately, the unworthy Huizong spent the palace reserves on the Genyue pleasure garden, after which the Jin invaded. The Ming needs no elaboration: its Board of Revenue was desperately poor while palace wealth piled high, only to fall into the rebels' hands. Our dynasty is different. Reserves are held in the state treasury, not the Imperial Household Department.”

zh: 接着王有龄便举了几个户部存银的数目，康熙四十八年到过五千万两，最后剩下八百万两，但雍正十三年的极力整顿，到乾隆即位时，库存到了前所未有的六千万两的巨数，以后乾隆四十六年，到过七千万两。但嘉庆以后就不行了，到道光朝更是每况愈下。“先帝崩逝当时，户部存银八百万两，这三年来的数目不详。洪杨军兴以来，用财如流水，想来现在正是开国以来最穷的时候。”
en: Wang then cited treasury balances: fifty million taels in Kangxi's forty-eighth year, falling to eight million by the end; after thirteen years of vigorous reform under Yongzheng, an unprecedented sixty million at Qianlong's accession; and seventy million in Qianlong's forty-sixth year. After Jiaqing, however, the position deteriorated, worsening further under Daoguang. “When the late emperor died, the Board held eight million taels. I don't know the figures for the last three years. Since Hong and Yang rose, money has flowed like water. I imagine the dynasty has never been poorer.”

zh: 这一番夹叙夹议的谈论，不但周、吴等人有茅塞顿开之感，就是杨用之也觉得长了一番见闻。钱谷一道虽是他的专业，却只了解一隅之地的财政，朝廷大藏，十分隔膜，现在听王有龄讲得头头是道，心里便有这样一个想法：这位东翁，莫道他是捐班出身，肚子里着实有些货色。他想到了王有龄的出身，王有龄恰好也要谈到捐班，“弥补国用不足，再有一个办法是靠捐纳的收入。”他说，“捐官的制度，起于汉朝，即所谓‘纳赀为郎’。此后历代都有，但不如本朝的盛行。”接着，王有龄便细谈清朝捐纳制度演变的经过，以及对中枢岁收的关系。捐纳实缺虽由康熙为三藩之乱，筹措军费而起，但至雍正朝即成为“常例”，捐纳收入几为国家岁收的一部分，只是比例不大，平均总在百分之十五左右。捐例之滥，始于嘉庆朝，它的收入常为岁收的一半，嘉庆七年那一年，更高达岁收总额百分之八十以上。“捐例一滥，其弊不可胜言。”王有龄泰然说道，“我自己虽是捐班出身，但也实在叫我无法看得起捐班的。只要有钱，不管什么胸无点墨的人，都可以做官。做官既要先花本钱，那就跟做生意一样，一补上实缺，先要捞回本息。请问吏治如何澄清得来？”
en: The mixture of narrative and analysis enlightened not only Zhou and Wu but Yang himself. Revenue was his profession, yet he knew only local finance and little of the central treasury. Hearing Wang explain it so coherently, he thought that, purchased qualification or not, his employer had considerable learning. At that very moment Wang turned to purchased office. “The second way to meet a public shortfall is through contributions paid for official qualifications. The system began under the Han, when money could obtain a position as a palace gentleman. Later dynasties retained it, but none used it as extensively as ours.” He described its development and connection with central revenue. Contributions for actual appointments had begun under Kangxi to fund the war against the Three Feudatories. By Yongzheng's reign they had become a regular practice, their proceeds effectively part of annual revenue, though at a relatively modest average of around fifteen per cent. Excessive use began under Jiaqing. The proceeds often equalled half the year's revenue, and in his seventh year exceeded eighty per cent. “Once the system is abused, its evils are beyond description,” Wang said evenly. “Though I myself entered by purchase, I can hardly respect that class of official. Anyone with money, however ignorant, can obtain office. Having first invested capital, he treats administration like a business. Once appointed, he must recover principal and interest. How can clean government result?”

zh: “这也不可一概而论。”吴委员说，“赴试登进，自是正途，但‘场中莫论文’，要靠‘一命、二运、三风水’，所以怀才不遇的也多的是。捐例开了方便之门，让他们有个发挥机会，不致埋没人才，也是莫大功德之事。”这是在暗中恭维王有龄，他当然听得懂，而且也不必客气，“象兄弟这种情形到底不多。”他说，“纵有一利，奈有百害何？如今为了军费，越发广开已滥的捐例，搞得满街是官，那还成何话说！”“东翁见得极是。”杨用之倒是真的心悦诚服，所以不自觉其矛盾地改了论调，“本朝的商税，原就不重，杂赋中的牙帖税、当税、牲畜税以外，买卖的商税，只有买别地货物到店发卖的‘落地税’，也就是‘坐税’。至于货物经过的‘过税’，只有关税一种，如今酌增厘捐，亦不为过。”“就是这话罗！”王有龄口中这样在说，心中却己想到厘捐是否亦可在浙江开办？
en: “That cannot be said of everyone,” Wu objected. “Advancement by examination is naturally the proper path. But examination success doesn't depend on writing alone. Fate, luck, and favourable circumstances play their part, leaving many capable men unrecognised. Purchase opens a door through which they can exercise their talents instead of being buried. That too is a great service.” The compliment to Wang was implicit and understood. He saw no need to disclaim it. “Cases like mine are uncommon. Even one advantage cannot compensate for a hundred harms. Now military expenses are widening an already overused system until the streets are full of officials. What sense does that make?” “Your view is entirely sound,” Yang answered, sincerely convinced. Without noticing his reversal, he changed his argument. “Commercial taxes in our dynasty are not heavy. Apart from such miscellaneous charges as brokers' licence fees, pawnshop duties, and livestock taxes, ordinary trade pays only the tax on goods brought from elsewhere for sale in local shops—the landing tax, also called the stationary tax. Goods in transit pay only customs duties. A moderate additional lijin levy would not be excessive.” “Precisely!” Wang said, already wondering privately whether Zhejiang too might introduce it.

zh: 一场议论，算是有了结果。胡雪岩换了个话题，他很佩服钱江，所以这样发问：“杨老夫子可识得那位钱先生？”“你是说钱江？”杨用之答道，“我们不但认识，而且还沾些亲。他字秋平，又字东平。祖上曾做过山东巡抚，他老太爷也在山东做过官，此人从小不凡，样样聪敏，就是不喜欢做八股文章。”“那怎么称做‘奇士’呢？”吴委员笑道，“象这样的人，必是不中绳墨，别有抱负的。”“他还有一策，现在各省都已仿行。”杨用之忽然看着胡雪岩说，“雪岩兄大可一办！”“请问，办什么？”胡雪岩愕然相问。“也是钱东平的主意，请旨预领空白捐照，随捐随发，人人称便，所以‘生意’好得很。”杨用之笑道，“本省亦已照样进行。雪岩兄大可捐个前程。”
en: The discussion had achieved its purpose. Hu changed the subject. Impressed by Qian Jiang, he asked whether Yang knew him. “Not only do I know him; we're distantly related. His courtesy names are Qiuping and Dongping. An ancestor was governor of Shandong, and his father also served there. He was exceptional from childhood, quick at everything except that he disliked eight-legged essays.” “How else would he be an extraordinary man?” Wu laughed. “Someone like that must disregard conventional restraints and have ambitions of his own.” “He proposed another measure now being adopted across the provinces.” Yang suddenly looked at Hu. “You could make use of it yourself.” “What measure?” “Another of Qian Dongping's ideas: obtain imperial permission to draw blank qualification certificates in advance and issue them as soon as contributions are paid. Everyone finds it convenient, so ‘business’ is excellent. This province has begun doing the same. You could purchase a qualification.”

zh: 这话倒把胡雪岩说动了，这几个月他在官场打了几个滚，深知“身分”二字的重要，倒不是为了炫耀，而是为了方便，无论拜客还是客人来拜，彼此请教姓氏时，称呼照规矩来，毫无窒碍。是个“白丁”，便处处有格格不入之感，熟人无所谓，大家可以称兄道弟，若是陌生的官儿，称呼上不是委屈了自己，就是得罪了别人，实在是一大苦事。因此，这天晚上他特地跟王有龄去商量。王有龄自然赞成：“我早就劝你快办了！我真不知道你什么意思？一直拖着。”“都是为了没工夫，”胡雪岩说，“这件事麻烦得很，费辰光不说，还有层层挑剔需索，把人的兴致都消磨光了。象现在这样。随捐随发，一手交钱，一手取照，自然又当别论。”“需索还是会有的。讲是讲‘随捐随发’，到底也没有那么快。不过，部照不必到部里去领，当然快得多。”
en: That appealed to Hu. His recent experience in official circles had taught him the importance of standing, not for display but for convenience. When making or receiving calls and exchanging names, a recognised qualification settled the proper forms of address without awkwardness. As an untitled commoner, he felt out of place everywhere. Friends could address one another as brothers, but with unfamiliar officials he risked either diminishing himself or offending them. It was a serious difficulty. That evening he specially consulted Wang, who naturally approved. “I've urged you to do it for ages! I don't know why you've kept delaying.” “No time. The business is troublesome. Apart from the time it takes, there are objections and demands for fees at every stage, enough to destroy anyone's enthusiasm. Immediate issue, with money handed over and the certificate received in return, is different.” “There will still be demands. ‘Immediate’ won't be quite so immediate. But avoiding collection from the ministry itself will certainly make it much faster.”

zh: “于此可见，凡事总要动脑筋。说到理财，到处都是财源。”胡雪岩又得到启示：“一句话，不管是做官的对老百姓，做生意的对主顾。 你要人荷包里的钱，就要把人伺候得舒服，才肯心甘情愿掏荷包。”“这话有道理。”王有龄深深点点，“我这趟到湖州，也要想办法把老百姓‘伺候’得舒舒服服，好叫他们高高兴兴来完钱粮。”“其实老百姓也很好问候，不打官腔，实事求是，老百姓自会说你是好官。”胡雪岩又谈到他自己的事，“雪公，你看我捐个什么班子？”“州县。”王有龄毫不考虑地答说，“这件事你托杨用之好了。”胡雪岩受了他的教，第二天特地具个柬帖，把杨用之请了在馆子里小酌。
en: “That shows how necessary it is to think. In finance, opportunities are everywhere.” Hu drew another lesson. “Whether an official dealing with the people or a merchant dealing with customers, if you want the money in their purses, make them comfortable enough to open those purses willingly.” “There's truth in that.” Wang nodded thoughtfully. “At Huzhou, I too must find a way to ‘serve’ the people comfortably, so they'll gladly pay their taxes.” “They're easy enough to serve. Avoid official bluster and deal with realities; they'll call you a good official.” Hu returned to his own business. “What qualification should I purchase?” “Department or county magistrate,” Wang answered without hesitation. “Entrust it to Yang Yongzhi.” Taking his advice, Hu sent Yang a formal invitation the next day and entertained him at a restaurant.

zh: 酒过三巡，谈起正事，杨用之一诺无辞，而且声叫：“报捐向来在正项以外，另有杂费，经手的人都有好处，我的一份扣除，杂费还可以打个七折。”“这不好。君子爱财，取之有道，该当你老夫子的，自然当仁不让。”“那还叫朋友吗？”杨用之摇着手说，“你不必管这一层了。我且问你的意思，光是捐个班呢，还是要捐‘花样’？”捐官的花样极多，最起码的是捐个空头名义，凭一张部照。就算是有了身分，可以光大门楣，炫耀乡里，如果要想补实缺。另有种种优先次序，补缺省份的花样。胡雪岩别有奥援，也不想进京到吏部报供候选。捐官不过捐个“胡老爷”的尊称，依旧开自己的钱庄，那就无须多加花费，另捐花样了。于是胡雪岩说：“我只要有张‘部照’就可以了。难道真的去做官？”“你要做官也不难，而且必是一等一的红员。不过人各有志。你明天就送银子来，我替你‘上兑’，尽快把捐照领下来。”
en: After three rounds of wine, they discussed the matter. Yang readily agreed and made an announcement. “Beyond the prescribed contribution, there are always miscellaneous charges from which everyone handling the business receives a benefit. I'll deduct my own share and reduce the miscellaneous fees by thirty per cent.” “That won't do. A gentleman may love money, provided he acquires it properly. Whatever is due to you should be accepted without hesitation.” “Would that be friendship?” Yang waved his hand. “Leave that to me. What I need to know is whether you want the basic qualification or additional preferences.” There were many variations in purchasing office. The simplest was an empty title supported by a ministry certificate, conferring standing, family distinction, and local prestige. An actual appointment required choices concerning priority and the province in which one would serve. Hu had other powerful support and no wish to travel to the capital, register with the Board of Civil Office, and await selection. He merely wanted the title “His Honour Hu” while continuing to run his bank. Additional expenditure was unnecessary. “I only need the ministry certificate. Am I really going to be an official?” “It wouldn't be difficult, and you'd be a favourite of the first order. But each man has his ambitions. Bring the silver tomorrow. I'll pay it in and obtain the certificate as quickly as possible.”

zh: “拜托，拜找！”胡雪岩道过谢，就不再提这事了，殷殷劝酒，一面拉拢杨用之，一面向他讨教州县钱谷出入之际，有些什么“花样”？杨用之人虽老实，而且也觉得他极够朋友，但遇到这些地方，他也不肯多说。好在胡雪岩机警，举一反三，依旧“偷”到不少“决窍”。第二天他从准备开钱庄的五千两银子中，提出一笔捐官的钱来，“正项”打成票子，“杂费”是现银，一起送到杨用之那里。杨用之果然不肯受好处。把杂费中他应得的一份退了回来。
en: Hu thanked him and said no more about the purchase. He diligently pressed wine upon Yang, strengthening their friendship while asking what opportunities existed around local revenue receipts and expenditure. Honest though Yang was, and warmly as he regarded Hu, he would not say much on those matters. Hu's quick understanding nevertheless enabled him to infer several methods from the hints he received. The next day, he took the purchase money from the five thousand taels set aside for opening the bank. The official contribution was made into a draft, the miscellaneous charges supplied in silver, and both delivered to Yang. True to his word, Yang returned the portion of the fees that would have been his own benefit.
